steps.description: Traveller reports missed KUL->SIN connection (pack msg-ait-s2-001); explicit elementId because the report lands after the leg's scheduled departure (DR-7 seam)

body.travellerReport: Hi - stuck in KL. My flight out of Sydney left about five hours late (weather holding) and I missed my connection to Singapore. The airline desk rebooked me on a flight tomorrow morning at 8:10, landing just after 9. I present at the hackathon finals tomorrow afternoon and I am supposed to be at the lab in the morning too. My suitcase went on the morning flight apparently. What do we do?

assert.description: the missed-flight report opens a recovery case in the assessing state
the engine resolves the reported missed KUL->SIN leg as the disruption subject
the disruption signal is derived from the missed element, not hand-built
the impact engine classifies the disruption severity deterministically
the impact assessment names direct failures
blast radius: the missed leg itself is the direct failure the downstream propagation starts from

steps.description: Observe opened recovery case: downstream impact propagated from the missed leg to every dependent engagement

assert.description: the case belongs to the reporting traveller's trip
the case reflects a traveller-originated state change awaiting recovery

assert.expected: Traveller reported missing a scheduled flight
assert.description: the case carries the deterministic what-changed narrative
the affected item is the missed transport leg
the missed leg propagates to all three dependent commitments (hackathon lab, finals, awards)
the first downstream engagement constraint is evaluated
with the KUL->SIN leg cancelled, arrival can no longer precede the first commitment
the second dependent engagement fails the same arrival constraint
the third dependent engagement fails the same arrival constraint

steps.description: Deterministic fallback planner re-searches the missed corridor (REPLAY recording) and the viability engine judges every replacement against the programme arrival constraints

assert.description: the planner requests corridor evidence first, then proposes from it
the evidence request is a flight search on the missed KUL->SIN corridor
the REPLAY recording supplied reprotection offers
every normalized corridor offer becomes a candidate rebook strategy
the cheaper late-morning replacement is deterministically infeasible
the rejection comes from a HARD constraint evaluation
the arrival gap verdict is FAIL, not UNKNOWN
the 10:40 departure lands after the hackathon lab starts: deterministic gap arithmetic
even the early-morning replacement fails the programme arrival-gap requirement
the 09:05 arrival leaves only 130min before the lab: below the required 360min buffer
hard-infeasible candidates can never win: no best strategy is ranked
the deterministic fallback planner records its own role honestly
the case advanced through the planning stage

steps.description: The trip read model reflects the disruption and the engine's viability verdict for the remainder

assert.description: the trip carries the traveller-originated disruption state

assert.expected: Traveller reported missing a scheduled flight
assert.description: the trip narrative matches the signal's what-changed copy
downstream impact: with the KUL->SIN leg cancelled the remaining itinerary is deterministically not viable

steps.description: The authoritative mutation trail shows the traveller report applied before the signal pipeline assessed impact

assert.description: the planning, mutation and signal-processing trail is recorded
the planning loop's outcome is recorded on the trip trail
the missed-leg state change was applied to authoritative trip state
the mutation is attributed to the reporting traveller, not the system
the disruption signal was processed through the generic signal pipeline
